subject: Assurance & evidence: high-risk AI use case — NIST / EU AI Act + regression plan
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@auroramed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: AuroraMed Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifications: evidence & conformity for high-risk use case

Karthik,

Thanks for the RFP response draft — the AuroraMed team reviewed the high-level materials and we have a few targeted clarifications so we can proceed with our internal conformity assessment under the EU AI Act (high-risk device integration) and map to NIST AI RMF expectations. Please provide concise, evidentiary responses to the items below. Where possible, attach the artifacts (reports/spreadsheets) rather than links.

1) Conformity pathway: Do you treat our integration (clinical decision support assisting radiologists) as a high-risk product under the EU AI Act? If so, what conformity assessment route do you anticipate (internal control + third-party testing, or full external conformity assessment)?

2) NIST mapping: We need a mapping table showing which NIST AI RMF subcategories you meet and where mitigations live (product/runtime/policy).

3) Regression & eval plan: Please describe your regression test cadence, sampling approach (how many prompts/clinical vignettes per release), and acceptance thresholds for generation quality. Include any continuous-monitoring triggers that would block a rollout.

4) Red-team & adversarial testing: Do you run targeted red-team tests for hallucinations and safety-critical failures? Please include a recent executive summary of results (redacted if necessary).

5) Evidence catalogue: Provide an evidence index (artifact name, owner, retention policy, last-updated).

6) Data residency & logs: For dedicated/private deployments, what logs are retained, for how long, and what is available for audits (KV cache, request/response tokens)?

7) Compliance accreditations: SOC 2 type II, penetration test cadence, encryption at rest/in transit details.

If you can get us a consolidated PDF for AuroraMed that we can attach to our conformity assessment packet by Friday (2027-03-12), that would be ideal. Otherwise, a short call to walk through would work.

Regards,
Elena
Procurement Manager
AuroraMed

--

Attachment request: latest red-team executive summary (PDF) and the evidence-catalogue spreadsheet
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifications: evidence & conformity for high-risk use case

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together the artifacts below and attached a consolidated PDF tailored to AuroraMed's inquiry. Summary of what you'll find attached:

- Redwood_AuroraMed_Assurance_Response_20270312.pdf — high-level narrative answers mapped to your seven points, plus owner contacts for each artifact.
- evidence-catalogue-auroramed-20270312.xlsx — indexed evidence (artifact, owner, retention, last updated).
- eval-regression-sampling-plan-20270312.md — our recommended regression cadence and sampling approach for clinical-grade rollouts.

Key notes (concise):
- Conformity pathway: We recommend a combined approach for this integration — internal conformity controls (documentation, test harnesses, model cards) plus third-party conformity assessment for the final CE marking if AuroraMed classifies the overall product as high-risk. Redwood can support evidence packaging and a third-party assessor handoff.

- NIST mapping: The attached PDF includes a NIST AI RMF mapping table and where controls are implemented (runtime, infra, product config). For example, detection of distribution drift and automatic rollback is implemented in the Redwood runtime (rule-based and model-quality trigger).

- Regression cadence & sampling: Our default for clinical high-risk integrations is:
  * Pre-release: deterministic regression on a curated set of 1,200 vignettes + 3,000 randomized prompts derived from customer data schemas (anonymized).
  * Post-release continuous sampling: 500 prompts/day aggregated, with weekly metric computation (calibration, hallucination rate, safety violations).
  * Blockers: If hallucination rate or critical-safety violation rate increases by >0.5 percentage points vs. baseline or any single critical safety failure occurs in production sample, the system triggers automatic rollback and notifies SOC/CS teams.

- Red-team: We run quarterly adversarial exercises focused on domain-specific failure modes. We can share an executive summary (redacted) — attached in the PDF.

- Logs & data residency: For private/dedicated customers, logs (request/response, metadata, token counts, timestamps, and trace IDs) are retained per the contract. Default retention: 90 days; extended retention available for enterprise contracts. KV-cache contents are never persisted to customer-facing logs; audit captures cache misses/hits and cache key hashes only.

- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II + annual penetration tests; encryption TLS1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. We include a penetration test summary and SOC 2 attestation in the evidence catalogue.

Marissa & Grace: looping you in for product/legal language and to confirm the sampling plan wording — any adjustments before I send this formally to AuroraMed?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_AuroraMed_Assurance_Response_20270312.pdf; evidence-catalogue-auroramed-20270312.xlsx; eval-regression-sampling-plan-20270312.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:06:00 -0700

Karthik — this looks good. Two requested edits before we send to the customer packet:

1) EU AI Act wording: please add one paragraph indicating Redwood's role as a component supplier vs. the overall medical device manufacturer. Emphasize we provide evidence and tooling for conformity but that the ultimate CE conformity pathway is determined by AuroraMed (manufacturer).

2) Regression thresholds: tighten the wording on rollback triggers to indicate an initial grace period during the first 48 hours of a rollout (monitored, but not auto-rollback unless a critical safety failure is observed). That aligns better with our staged canary policy.

I attached a short clause we typically include for EU AI Act high-risk declarations (see attached clause snippet). Also confirm the sampling numbers are defensible — if the customer wants an accelerated pre-release sweep we can recommend a one-time expansion of randomized prompts.

Thanks — Marissa
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

Changes since my earlier note: we included the EU AI Act supplier clause and clarified the staged canary policy (48-hour monitored grace window, auto-rollback only for critical safety incidents) as Marissa requested. The packet contents are:

- Redwood_AuroraMed_Assurance_Response_20270312.pdf (consolidated narrative + NIST mapping table + redacted red-team executive summary)

Quick highlights for your conformity packet:
- Conformity pathway recommendation: Combined internal controls + third-party conformity assessment for CE marking. Redwood will prepare handoff materials for assessors.
- NIST AI RMF: Our mapping attaches controls to product (model card, retraining gates), runtime (monitoring, drift detection, rollback), and org (incident response, policy).
- Regression sampling: Pre-release deterministic set (1,200 vignettes) + randomized augment (3,000 anonymized prompts) and continuous sampling 500/day. Acceptance: calibration and hallucination metrics must remain within baseline +/-0.5pp; any single critical safety failure triggers immediate investigation and rollback. During initial 48-hour canary, teams monitor closely and will only auto-rollback if a critical failure is observed.
- Evidence & artifacts: SOC 2 Type II attestation, latest pen-test summary, redacted red-team executive summary, test harness outputs, and model cards.

Next steps: Would you like a 45-minute technical review with our product and security owners early next week to walk through the packet and answer assessor questions? We can also provide expanded sampling results on request.
